Educational steady-state model over flat terrain. Direction is meteorological FROM, clockwise from true north. Prevailing and uniform random modes use 1,200 reproducible intervals (seed 22001); prevailing uses a 40° standard deviation and random ignores the entered direction. The recommended manual table requires direction_from_deg (degrees), wind_speed_m_s (m/s, greater than zero), and frequency_percent (nonnegative with a positive total). Frequencies are normalized. Calm periods must be excluded and documented separately. Each direction produces a plume and the output is its weighted mean. Effective height is supplied by the user. Terrain, deposition, chemistry, buildings, and plume rise are not represented.

Educational steady-state model over flat terrain. Direction is meteorological FROM, clockwise from true north. Prevailing and uniform random modes use 1,200 reproducible intervals (seed 22001); prevailing uses a 40° standard deviation and random ignores the entered direction. The observation table requires timestamp_utc (ISO 8601 UTC), direction_from_deg (degrees), and wind_speed_m_s (m/s, greater than zero). Each row represents an equal-duration interval. The rose uses 16 sectors; calculation groups observations into 72 direction sectors and seven speed classes before averaging the plumes. Calm periods must be excluded and documented separately. The entered height is the physical stack height; plume rise is assumed to be zero and effective height equals it. Terrain, deposition, chemistry, buildings, and plume rise are not represented.

Modelo docente estacionario sobre terren: Educational steady-state model over flat terrain based on Masters and Ela (2008). Wind direction is meteorological FROM, clockwise from true north. Prevailing and uniform random modes use 1,200 reproducible intervals (seed 22001); prevailing uses a 40° standard deviation and random ignores the entered direction. The observation table requires timestamp_utc (ISO 8601 UTC), direction_from_deg (degrees), and wind_speed_m_s (m/s, greater than zero). Each row represents an equal-duration interval. The rose uses 16 sectors; the calculation groups observations into 72 direction sectors and seven speed classes before averaging the plumes. Calm periods must be excluded and documented separately. Wind speed is adjusted from the measurement height to the stack and dispersion uses the Martin equations. The entered height is the physical stack height; plume rise is assumed to be zero and effective height equals it. Terrain, deposition, chemistry, buildings, and plume rise are not represented.
